environment.description: Same Quarkus 3.2 application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate in a private subnet with no internet gateway or NAT gateway attached. Service is exposed exclusively through an interface VPC endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) with endpoint policy restricting to principal arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/AllowedConsumerRole. The VPC endpoint's associated security group permits inbound TCP 443 only from CIDR 10.0.0.0/16 (consumer VPC peered range). There is NO load balancer in front of the service — the NLB target group associated with the VPC endpoint service operates at Layer 4 (TCP passthrough) and the Vert.x HTTP server in Quarkus handles TLS termination directly with HTTP/2 (h2) negotiated via ALPN. The Vert.x server configuration sets quarkus.http.http2=true and quarkus.http.http2-only=true, meaning HTTP/1.1 connections are rejected at the TLS handshake level. HTTP/2 uses binary framing with explicit stream multiplexing and does not support Transfer-Encoding: chunked as a hop-by-hop mechanism — Content-Length is authoritative and enforced per-stream by the h2 codec. Additionally, the VPC endpoint has a resource policy that denies any request not signed with SigV4 from the allowed principal.
